name: Dark Sea Green
lede: Dark Sea Green is a soft, grayed green, listed in the X11 set.

sections.title: A listed color
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary lists DarkSeaGreen as an entry in the X11 Color Set, with hex code 8FBC8F [1]. It also appears in his list of greens, beside Dark Green and Dark Olive Green [2]. The name has a longer paper trail than most of the set: our records list Ridgway (1912) and the ISCC-NBS system (1955) alongside CSS and the xkcd list [3].

Its nearest neighbors among our names, by CIELAB distance, are [[malachite-green|Malachite Green]], [[eton-blue|Eton Blue]] and [[naiad|Naiad]] [5]. On a white page it reaches a contrast ratio of 2.15:1 [5].

sections.title: In paintings
sections.body: In our archive Dark Sea Green appears in 42 of 23,781 paintings, 0.18%, as photographed [4]. It is a mid-tone more often than anything else, in 35% of the 20 paintings where the within-painting reading finds it [4]. It peaks in the 1900s at 3.7 times the expected rate, but that rests on only 7 paintings, so treat it as a hint [4]. The earliest match is a work by Hans von Kulmbach from 1514; the early centuries are thin, so that is a floor and not a first [4].
